home_bed.ask: A comfy bed. Rest until morning and recover your Bytekin?

mom_morning.say: Good morning, {p}! There's toast. Don't eat the toast. It's not real toast. ...I mean, eat it. It's fine.
Mira's been waiting outside since sunrise. She says she's 'not waiting', she's 'standing with purpose'.

mom_met_mira.say: Professor Vale's workshop, huh? Tell him he still owes me a casserole dish.
And {p}... eat something before you go anywhere strange. Strange things are always worse on an empty stomach.

mom_after.say: Your Bytekin look worn out, sweetheart. And so do you.

no.say: Come home whenever you want. The kitchen light will be on. Probably the same one.

mira_intro.say: Did you see it? This morning? The clocks went 9:59, then 10:01. Forty-one times I've logged that. Forty-one!
Professor Vale said to bring you to his workshop. He's finally letting us help with Signal Ecology!
Which is, officially, 'the study of unusual electromagnetic behaviour in animals'. Unofficially it's the study of everything weird.
Race you there! Loser buys the first Patch Kit!

mira_intro.text: Press START to open the menu.

relay_locked.say: The Old Signal Relay's door is sealed. A faded plate reads: DECOMMISSIONED. Someone has underlined it twice.

vale_intro.say: And Mira. Early, as always. I could have predicted it. In fact I did. It's in a notebook.
Right. Signal Ecology. Publicly it means electromagnetic behaviour in animals. Strange fur. Odd migrations. Birds that fly in squares.
Privately... it means I have a spectrograph that has been humming the same note since the day you were born.
Lately the note has been drifting. Clocks skip. Radios say things nobody sent. Signs print words that aren't in any language.
And the animals have been *duplicating*. Briefly. Then unduplicating. I would very much like to know why.
That was the whole district. Every light in Rivermoor just went out.
And that... that is the Old Signal Relay. It's powering up. It hasn't had power in twenty years.
That's impossible. Stay here. Both of you. I mean it. I'll call someone.
You said 'stay here' like we don't know where the relay is. Come on, {p}!
{p}. If you must follow her... the relay's maintenance door will open when the tower is live. Don't touch anything glowing. Touch everything glowing carefully. Take this.
I'm right behind you. Probably. Possibly. Depending on stairs.

vale_intro.text: The Old Signal Relay is open!

then.say: Root Key 01. So the Node woke up for you. Good. That's... good.
About the man in the white coat. If he comes back, don't give him the Debugger. Please.
The relay's quiet again. Eerily quiet. I'd like you to look into the Node in Briarfield. Route 01, past the grass.

then.ask: Need to rest your Bytekin before you go?

else.say: The tower wasn't on when I woke up. It's on now. I do not like this at all.

relay1_glitch.say: For a second the hallway repeated. The same corridor, twice, stacked like a bad copy.
The floor tiles blinked out and back. A few did not come back.

relay2_enter.say: Over here, {p}! The door at the top is sealed.
Three plates on the floor. A triangle, a circle, a square. And that note by the rack. I stepped on the plates in random order and the floor *yelled* at me.

then.say: Triangle, circle, square. In that order. Like the first three words of a language.
Walk onto the plates in the order the note says. If you get it wrong the whole floor resets.

else.say: Read the note near the rack first. I'm not stepping on those plates again. They have a temper.

then.say: The note: 'When the signal flows, the tower wakes. TRIANGLE. CIRCLE. SQUARE.'

else.say: A scrap of paper taped to the rack. It reads:
'When the signal flows, the tower wakes. Triangle. Circle. Square. In that order, the way a message is first spoken. - V.'

ch0_core.say: The core room is wrong in a hundred small ways. Walls that lean. Light with no source.
Three small shapes flicker around the antenna core. They are tearing at it - or trying to hold it together. It's hard to tell.
A Null cat. A Loop worm. A Signal bird. Three Bytekin. At once. In a *relay*. I've only ever seen one in twenty years!
They're not attacking the core. They're trying to stabilize it... and it's tearing them apart. Neither of them can hold on much longer.
{p}. Take this. It's a DEBUGGER. It scans, indexes, and stabilizes Bytekin with CONTAIN. I built it for exactly this and was too much of a coward to try it.
Pick one of them and stabilize it. Walk up and press A. Quickly!
Dibs on whichever one you don't pick!

pick_nullcat.say: NULLCAT. Type NULL. A small black cat with pixels missing around its tail. Evasive. Disruptive. Curious.

pick_segbyte.say: SEGBYTE. Type LOOP. A segmented worm whose body doesn't quite connect. Multi-hit. Stacking. Stubborn.

pick_bitbird.say: BITBIRD. Type SIGNAL. A small blue bird whose wings sometimes show the wrong animation frame. Fast. Informed. Chatty.

after_pick.say: The other two flicker, look back at you for one frame, and blink out into the Signal.

core_tutorial.say: The antenna core spits out a glitching CACHEMOUSE - the relay's resident hoarder! It copied itself seven times on the way out.
A corrupted Cachemouse! {p} - FIGHT to wear it down, then CONTAIN it with the Debugger!
The core's monitor flickers. Letters scroll across it slowly.
...That wasn't in any log. Not a single one.
Vale. What was that? Did the relay just try to talk to us?
A glitch, Mira. Feedback from the core. Nothing more.
{p}. The Debugger just updated itself. FIELD SCAN is now online. Walk close to glittering spots and press A.
Hold on to that Debugger. You are, as far as I know, the first person who ever stabilized a Bytekin on purpose.
There's a Node in Briarfield, down Route 01, that's been acting up. Irrigation. Crops. Duplicating. The Debugger might be able to help.
I'll patch up here. Mira, go with them. And Mira - *don't* run off this time.

core_tutorial.text: Head south to Briarfield via Route 01!

vale_core_wait.say: Go on, {p}. Walk out slowly. Don't touch the antenna.

mira_core_wait.say: I'm not going anywhere. I'm taking notes. Many, many notes.

rivermoor_corruption.say: A hum runs through the town. Somewhere in the east, a patch of ground has gone the wrong colour.
Rivermoor looks a little less sure of itself.
